sections.h2: What are my options to sell a house in North Miami quickly?
sections.html:
You can sell to a cash buyer, list with an agent, or sell on your own, and the right choice depends on how soon you need to close and how much work the house needs. In North Miami the deed, the title search and Miami-Dade County's recording process are the same on every route. What changes is who pays for repairs, how long you wait and how much you keep.

  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you negotiate, usually with the house taken as is.
  • Agent listing: a wider buyer pool, with showings, an inspection period and a lender's schedule.
  • Owner sale: no listing fee, but you manage the contract, disclosures and screening.

Whichever route you pick, get at least two written numbers and compare what you would net, not the headline price.

sections.h2: What kind of city is North Miami?
sections.html:
North Miami is a suburban city in northeast Miami-Dade County, about ten miles north of downtown Miami, and its own communications describe it as the sixth largest city in the county with more than 64,000 residents. The city was incorporated on February 5, 1926, and it marked its centennial in 2026 with a year of events centered on downtown around NE 125th Street.

Biscayne Bay lies along its eastern side, and the Biscayne Bay Campus of Florida International University is nearby. The city also lists the Oleta River State Park, the largest urban park in the Florida State Park System, and the Museum of Contemporary Art at MOCA Plaza among its landmarks. Homes near the water and near the university draw different buyers than homes inland, and renters and investors are a steady part of the market.

Biscayne Boulevard runs through the city as its main commercial road, and the city sits near the county's north government center, which matters if you ever need to visit court or county offices in person.

sections.h2: What local rules should I check before I sell in North Miami?
sections.html:
Start with the code compliance office, because North Miami has a minimum housing and inspection program and its published answers cover parking, right-of-way upkeep and rentals. Its FAQ says violation notices go to the property owner, not the tenant, so an open violation on your address is your problem to clear before closing.

Rentals are tightly limited. The city's FAQ states that advertising a rental for less than three months is prohibited, and that renting for three months or less, or renting more than four times in a twelve month period, is prohibited. If your house has been used for short stays, a buyer will ask about it, and you should stop before listing.

  • Ask code compliance whether the address has open violations or an unfinished inspection.
  • Keep the right-of-way in front of the lot maintained, since owners are responsible for it.
  • Do not divide a single-family home into units without permits from the city's Building Department.
  • Ask whether a certificate of use or business tax receipt is attached to the property.

The city's code compliance phone line is listed on its site, and calling it before you list is cheaper than learning about a problem from the buyer's title company.

sections.h2: How much does a North Miami closing cost in taxes and fees?
sections.html:
Documentary stamp tax is the big state item, and Miami-Dade County has its own rate. The Florida Department of Revenue says Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax on deeds, and that the surtax does not apply to a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. Other counties charge 70 cents per $100.

Closing items on a North Miami deed, from official Florida pages
ItemWhat the official page says
Deed stamp tax, Miami-Dade60 cents per $100, plus 45 cents per $100 surtax (not due on a single-family dwelling only)
Liability for the taxAll parties to the document are liable
Clerk recording, first page$5.00
Clerk recording, each added page$4.00
Where tax is paidTo the county clerk at recording

The statute also lists small extra charges per page, so the title company's settlement statement is the place to see the final recording total. Mortgage payoffs, association fees and prorated property tax come out of your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How do Miami-Dade property taxes work for a North Miami seller?
sections.html:
The county property appraiser sets the value as of January 1 and the tax collector bills in November. The state calendar has the proposed tax notice going out in August, and the Miami-Dade appraiser's homestead page says exemption applications are due March 1 and late ones are accepted until the deadline printed on the proposed notice, usually 25 days after it is mailed.

The homestead exemption belongs to you, not the house. When you sell, the buyer files a new application, and a sale resets the assessed value to market level the following January 1. The appraiser's page also warns that renewal receipts are not sent to properties with a change of ownership, including by warranty or quitclaim deed.

The same page describes Amendment 3, approved by Florida voters on November 3, 2026, which raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 for tax year 2027 and $250,000 for 2028 for owners who established residency by December 31, 2026. A buyer's future bill may look quite different from yours, so ask a title or tax professional before you make claims about it in a listing.

sections.h2: Can I sell an inherited or tenant occupied house in North Miami?
sections.html:
Yes, but you need the authority to sign the deed, and a tenant's lease continues unless it ends. For an inherited house, the buyer's title company will want letters from the probate court or proof that the property passed outside probate. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not subject to stamp tax.

For a house with a tenant, give the buyer the lease and the deposit details. A cash buyer may accept the tenant, or may ask that the unit be vacant at closing. Because North Miami limits short rentals, confirm that the use is lawful before you describe it to a buyer.

Florida requires a deed to be signed before two witnesses. Quitclaim deeds are taxable documents too, so moving a house to a relative before a sale can add cost and may change how the county treats ownership.

sections.h2: What is a sensible timeline for a sale in North Miami?
sections.html:
A cash sale can be as short as a couple of weeks if the title is clean, while a financed sale usually takes longer because of the appraisal and loan approval. Build in time for payoff letters, an association estoppel if the home is in a community, and any permit or violation clearing.

  • Week one: gather the deed, tax bill, payoff and any association papers.
  • Next: compare offers and choose a closing date.
  • Then: title search, clearing of liens or violations, and scheduling the signing.
  • Closing: sign before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records the deed.

Contracts written with a firm closing date and a clear list of seller repairs avoid the most common delays.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax rate on a deed in North Miami?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade County uses 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, according to the Florida Department of Revenue. The surtax is not due on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. Your title company can give the exact number for your deed.

faqs.q: Can I rent my North Miami house for a few weeks to cover the mortgage while it is listed?
faqs.a: The city's published answer says rentals of three months or less are prohibited and that more than four rentals in twelve months is prohibited. Check with code compliance before you list the home for any short stay.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must apply with the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1 for the year in which he or she wants the exemption. The sale also resets the assessed value to market level the next January 1.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for a code violation notice at my address?
faqs.a: The city addresses the notice to the property owner. A tenant should speak with the landlord about obligations, but you should plan to clear the violation before closing.

faqs.q: What is Amendment 3 and when does it start?
faqs.a: According to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser, voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year, raising the non-school homestead exemption for eligible owners.
